audit.whatIsWrong: 8.5/10 is right; the chart under it was not.
audit.why: 48.18% over 467 games and the mirror rating this easy from Heimerdinger's side both point the same way — a hard lane where level 1 is the only free moment.
audit.corrected: Difficulty kept, level 1 restored to Olaf so the one window the reader can actually use is visible.

audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 0, 1, 3 and 5 disagreed with the packet and with the mirror.
audit.why: The mirror already moved rows 0 to Olaf, 1 to Skill, 3 to Heimerdinger and 5 to Heimerdinger in both layers, matching the packet chart — and matching this entry's own whys[0], which says you win the very first contact.
audit.corrected: Those four rows flipped as one atomic group across both layers, ratings moved with them.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four strings say Ragnarok 'cleanses' the CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade.
audit.why: Ragnarok does not cleanse. It grants immunity to disables for as long as he keeps attacking, on 100/90/80s — so the grenade's stun is nullified only while you are swinging, and only until the ultimate ends. The grenade is an 11s flat cooldown, which is why he can hold it for after your R.
audit.corrected: Restated as disable immunity while attacking, with the grenade's 11s written in.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four strings give Olaf's W lifesteal or omnivamp ('W sustain', 'W-sustain', 'W-omnivamp the turret damage', 'short-fight W sustain').
audit.why: Tough It Out is attack speed plus a SHIELD on 16/15/14/13/12s. Against constant turret and rocket chip that distinction decides the dive: a shield absorbs one burst, it does not out-heal a nest. The healing is the passive and scales with missing health.
audit.corrected: Split correctly everywhere — shield for the dive, missing-health passive for the sustain.

audit.whatIsWrong: The turret's real cost was never given a number.
audit.why: H-28 G Evolution Turret is a 1s cooldown on 20 mana with stored charges — the nest is not a cooldown you can wait out, which is why the advice must be about the 11s grenade instead.
audit.corrected: Grenade cooldown made the tracked number in breakdown.early and wants.you[1].

edits.before: Axe-slow + W sustain wins the first trades. Identify how Heimerdinger contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Undertow's slow into an auto wins first contact — before a second turret is planted he has no answer to a melee walk-up.

edits.before: Axe-slow + W sustain wins the first trades. Respect Heimerdinger's CH-2 Grenade completely — the first levels are about banking small advantages, not proving a point.
edits.after: Undertow's slow and Tough It Out's shield win first contact only. Once the nest is up, trade around the grenade's 11s — these levels are about surviving, not proving a point.

edits.before: Land the axe slow on Heimerdinger, walk the pickup for the reset, reave the true damage, and W-sustain whatever he answers with.
edits.after: Undertow him as he steps up, walk the pickup to reset its 9s, then Reckless Swing — Tough It Out shields the turret chip.

edits.after: Undertow him as he steps up, walk the pickup to reset its 9s, then Reckless Swing — Tough It Out shields the turret chip.

edits.after: Ragnarok's immunity holds off the grenade while you swing, but the turret nest still chunks the dive and he can wait R out.

edits.after: Ragnarok makes the grenade stun irrelevant while you keep swinging, but his turret nest still chunks you mid-dive.

edits.after: Save Ragnarok's 100s for the grenade, then keep swinging so the stun never lands

edits.before: Levels 4-6 he settles in: W rockets poke you under your own tower and the turret wall keeps your Q from ever sticking the slow. At 6 your Ragnarok cleanses his E stun-grenade, so that is the one window you actually get to commit — flash or dive in, Q-slow, W-omnivamp the turret damage, and E-nuke him. But honestly the nest still chunks you on the way in, and if he saves E for after your R duration you get walled right back out. You need a jungler to collapse with you; alone, you trade your health bar for one threat and he rebuilds the wall.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 he settles in: Hextech Micro-Rockets poke you under your own tower and the turret wall keeps Undertow from ever sticking the slow. At 6 Ragnarok holds off his grenade stun as long as you keep attacking, so that is the one window you commit — Flash or walk in, Undertow, Tough It Out for the shield, and Reckless Swing him. The nest still chunks you on the way in, and if he holds the 11s grenade for after R ends you get walled right back out. Bring your jungler; alone you trade a health bar for one turret.

edits.before: This is where it slips fully out of reach. Three upgraded turrets plus Liandry's/Rylai W rockets zone you off every objective, and your flat E true damage and short-fight W sustain stop mattering against a wall you cannot tank through. Your only path is baiting the E grenade and forcing a flank where his turrets are not set up, or letting your team pull his nest while you dive the carry behind it. Do not splitpush into his side lane — that is exactly the zoned chokepoint he is built to hold.
edits.after: This is where it slips fully out of reach. Three upgraded turrets plus Liandry's/Rylai rockets zone you off every objective, and Reckless Swing's flat true damage and your missing-health lifesteal stop mattering against a wall you cannot tank through. Your only path is baiting the grenade and flanking where his turrets are not set up, or letting your team pull the nest while you dive the carry behind it. Do not splitpush into his side lane — that is the chokepoint he is built to hold.

notes: Four strings had Ragnarok cleansing the grenade. It does not cleanse — it is disable immunity that lasts only while he keeps attacking, and the grenade is a flat 11s, which is exactly why holding it for after your ultimate is his best play and why the entry's own whys[4] was closer to right than its spikes[1]. Chart rows 0, 1, 3 and 5 flipped to the packet and the mirror; the page previously claimed Heimerdinger wins level 1 while its whys[0] said the opposite. Turret cooldown is 1s with mana as the real limit, so no advice here tells the reader to wait it out.
